title: LLM Data Retention: Platform Controls vs Custom Safeguards

steps.prompt: A bank will approve an Agentforce service agent on a third-party LLM only if the model provider retains no prompt data and does not train on it. Regulators also require a record of every inference call. What should the architect rely on to meet both requirements?

options.label: The Einstein Trust Layer controls applied to each third-party model call
options.rationale: The Trust Layer governs data in motion at inference time: zero data retention agreements mean providers keep nothing after inference and never use it for training, and audit events log each request with the controls applied. Both requirements are met without infrastructure the bank must build.

options.label: A customer-hosted proxy that tokenizes customer data before prompts leave Salesforce
options.rationale: The proxy is infrastructure the bank must run, yet it neither binds the provider’s retention and training terms nor records each inference call.

options.label: Automatic deletion of stored prompt transcripts from Salesforce when each session ends
options.rationale: Retention terms apply to the external model provider, not Salesforce; deleting in-org transcripts destroys the inference records regulators require and changes nothing the provider keeps.

options.label: Shield Platform Encryption on every Salesforce field the agent reads for grounding
options.rationale: Shield encrypts data at rest, but fields are decrypted when the agent reads them into a prompt, so the provider still receives the values and no inference call is logged.
